# Visual-quality benchmark

**Dataset:** `synthetic-planar-v1`, generated by [`benchmark/fixtures.py`](../benchmark/fixtures.py). Reproduce with:

```bash
python -m benchmark.run_benchmark --split all --out benchmark/results.json
```

Raw per-clip results: [`benchmark/results.json`](../benchmark/results.json). Policy evaluated: `planar-v0.1-heuristic`.

## What the dataset is, and is not

Each clip is 480×270, 25 fps, 3.2 s, with AAC audio. A virtual camera films a textured planar "poster" in a textured world. The world→image homography is known for every frame, which gives **exact geometric ground truth**. Every clip is labelled suitable or unsuitable **by construction, before evaluation**, and each unsuitable clip has an expected reason code. The placement interval is 0.4–2.8 s (61 frames) with the reference at 0.4 s.

It is legally unencumbered and reproducible, but synthetic:
- No real lighting, materials, reflections, compression artefacts from phones, rolling shutter, or human motion.
- Each class has 5 clips (2 dev + 3 test), which is far too few for tight error bounds.
- Clips use one resolution and frame rate.

**Synthetic results do not establish real-world false-acceptance rates.** They show that the gates behave as designed on the failure modes they model.

| Kind | Label | Expected code | Scene |
|---|---|---|---|
| static | suitable | – | Static camera (class A) |
| pan_zoom | suitable | – | Smooth pan and zoom (class B) |
| perspective | suitable | – | Changing viewing angle (class B) |
| handheld | suitable | – | Pan plus handheld jitter |
| sensor_noise | suitable | – | Heavy sensor noise |
| mild_lighting | suitable | – | ±8% brightness drift |
| cut_after | suitable | – | Scene cut after the interval |
| cut_inside | unsuitable | SCENE_CUT_IN_INTERVAL | Cut inside the interval |
| occluder | unsuitable | PARTIAL_OCCLUSION_UNSUPPORTED | Object crosses the surface (class C) |
| low_texture | unsuitable | LOW_TEXTURE | Flat surface |
| deforming | unsuitable | NON_PLANAR_OR_UNSTABLE | Surface ripples (class D) |
| exits_frame | unsuitable | PRODUCT_OUT_OF_FRAME | Surface leaves the frame |
| motion_blur | unsuitable | MOTION_BLUR_UNSUPPORTED | Strong blur (no blur synthesis) |
| lighting_change | unsuitable | LIGHTING_CHANGE_UNSUPPORTED | Brightness falls ~50% (no relighting) |

## Method
- **Split by source seed:** dev = seeds 0–1 (28 clips), test = seeds 2–4 (42 clips). Seeds produce different textures, jitter and occluders.
- **Thresholds were set from first principles before the first run.** The dev run returned 28/28 correct decisions, so no decision threshold was tuned. One *output-validation* threshold was changed on dev data (below). The policy was then frozen and the test split run once.
- For accepted clips the product quad is rendered, then the real output file is validated.

### The one dev-split adjustment
The first dev run failed output validation on 13/14 correct renders: product-region colour PSNR was 25–27 dB against a 26 dB threshold. Measurement showed this was 4:2:0 chroma subsampling on saturated product edges, not misplacement:

| Product region (luma PSNR) | Range on dev clips |
|---|---|
| Correct render | 33.7–37.8 dB |
| Product missing | ~11 dB |
| Product shifted by 3 px | 10–11 dB |

Validation now uses luma PSNR with a 28 dB threshold, which leaves a margin of at least 5 dB below correct renders and at least 17 dB above both defects.

## Results (held-out test split, frozen policy)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Clips | 42 (21 suitable, 21 unsuitable) |
| Correct accept/reject decisions | **42/42** |
| False acceptance (unsuitable accepted) | **0/21** (95% upper bound ≈ 14%, rule of three) |
| False rejection (suitable refused) | 0/21 |
| Rejections carrying the expected reason code | 18/21 |
| Product corner error vs ground truth, accepted clips | mean 0.39 px, max 2.94 px |
| Temporal jitter of the error (std of frame-to-frame change) | ≤ 0.083 px |
| Accepted renders whose output passed validation | 21/21 |
| Median quality analysis time per clip | 0.44 s (61 tracked frames at 480×270) |
| Median render / validation time (all accepted clips) | 0.58 s / 0.74 s |

Dev split (for reference): 28/28 decisions, 0/14 false accepts, 0/14 false rejects, 12/14 expected codes, max corner error 2.81 px, 14/14 outputs validated.

### Known misclassifications of the reason
All 5 `deforming` clips were correctly **rejected**, but as `TRACKING_DRIFT` (and on 2 clips also `PARTIAL_OCCLUSION_UNSUPPORTED`), not the expected `NON_PLANAR_OR_UNSTABLE`. The photometric check catches the ripple before the RANSAC residual crosses its threshold. The decision is safe; the explanation shown to the user is less precise than it should be.

## Interpretation and next steps
- The gates behave as designed on the modelled failure modes. Nothing here measures realism (lighting match, shadows, aesthetics), which is why human fit review stays mandatory.
- Before any pilot, build a real-footage set (target 50–100 clips across creators and devices, split by creator). Re-measure false acceptance and set thresholds per scene class from it.
- Add classes not yet covered: reflective and specular surfaces, rolling shutter, compression-heavy phone footage, curved surfaces, multiple similar textures (aperture problem), low light with noise and gain.
